starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.speaker: Chancellor Hassan
starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.text: Greetings! I am Hassan, Chancellor to the Emir of Al Kharid.

options.text: Is there anything I can help you with?

steps.player: Is there anything I can help you with?

steps.speaker: Chancellor Hassan
steps.text: Well... we do currently have a very urgent issue we need to resolve, and I suppose you look like someone who knows how to get a job done. Are you definitely interested in helping?

steps.prompt: Start the Prince Ali Rescue quest?

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: Of course.

steps.speaker: Chancellor Hassan
steps.text: You'll find our Spymaster, Osman, just outside the palace. Go to him and tell him I sent you. He will fill you in on the details of our problem.

steps.player: Alright, I'll get to it.

options.text: No.

steps.player: Actually, I've changed my mind.

steps.speaker: Chancellor Hassan
steps.text: I see. Well you know where to find me if you do wish to help us.

options.text: It's just too hot here. How can you stand it?
Do you mind if I just kill your warriors?
I'd better be off.

starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.speaker: Chancellor Hassan
starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.text: Hello again. Have you spoken to Osman yet? He should be just outside the palace.

starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.player: Not yet. I'll go and see him.

starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.speaker: Chancellor Hassan
starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.text: Hello again. I hear you have agreed to help rescue Prince Ali. On behalf of the Emir, I will have a reward ready for you upon your success.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: Osman? I was told by the Chancellor to come and speak to you. Apparently you have an issue that I can help with.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: That would be an apt description. However, I find you to be an interesting choice by the Chancellor. Why has he chosen to trust you with this task over one of our own?

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: Er... I just asked if he needed help and he said yes.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: That man is far too trusting at a time when we must take extra care. However, if he has made his decision, I will not question it. Still, you should know that I will be keeping a close eye on you.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: Fair enough. So what is this issue?

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: Prince Ali, heir to the Emir of Al Kharid, has been taken. My spies have already discovered where he is being held, but we need someone to make the rescue.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: Well I'm sure I can manage that. How do I go about rescuing him?

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: The Prince has been taken by a group of bandits led by the self-proclaimed 'Lady' Keli. They are holding him in the abandoned jail just east of Draynor Village.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: According to our information, Keli is the only one able to freely move around the area. For you to get the Prince out, you will need to disguise him as her. She will of course need dealing with first.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: Why can't I just go in and kill her and her bandits?

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: And endanger the life of the Prince in the process? No. There will be no unnecessary risks. We need to do this with as little bloodshed as possible.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: You make a fair point. Do you know what Keli looks like?

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: She has blonde hair and wears pink clothes. My daughter, Leela, one of my spies, is currently in Draynor Village keeping an eye on the jail. I'm sure she can help you with the specifics.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: Before you go, there is one more thing. You'll need a key to get the Prince out of his cell. Keli has the only one. You could steal it, but that seems like a risk we should avoid.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: But if she has the only copy, and I can't just steal it, how do I get the key?

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: If you bring me an imprint of the key along with a bronze bar, I can show you how to make a copy. You should be able to make an imprint of the key using some soft clay.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: Of course, you'll need to find a way to get Keli to show you the key without causing suspicion. I'm sure Leela can help you with that.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: Sounds like I should head on over to Draynor Village and see Leela then.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: Indeed. Do you have any further questions before you go?

options.text: Do you know why they've taken the Prince?

steps.player: Do you know why they've taken the Prince?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: No, but we have our theories.

steps.player: Care to share them?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: No. You have not yet proven yourself enough to be trusted with that information.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Now, do you have any further questions?

options.text: Where abouts in Draynor is Leela?

steps.player: Where abouts in Draynor is Leela?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: She will be somewhere near the abandoned jail that the bandits are using. It's just east of the village.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Do you have any further questions?

options.text: No. I think I know everything I need to.

steps.player: No. I think I know everything I need to.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Then you should get going.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: You again. How are things going in Draynor?
If the player has the key imprint but no bronze bar:

steps.player: I have an imprint of the key.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Good. Bring me a bronze bar, and I'll get a copy made.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player has the key imprint and a bronze bar:

steps.player: I have an imprint of the key.

steps.text: You give Osman the imprint along with a bronze bar.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: I'll use this to have a copy of the key made. I'll send it to Leela once it's ready.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player has not acquired the key imprint:

steps.player: I'm still working on gathering all the items I need.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Well if you need help, just talk to Leela.

options.text: Do you know why they've taken the Prince?
Where abouts in Draynor is Leela?
I'll get going.

steps.player: I'll get going.

starting-out-talking-to-leela.player: You must be Leela. Your father sent me to help rescue Prince Ali.

starting-out-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
starting-out-talking-to-leela.text: Yes, he sent word ahead that you'd be coming. Are you aware of the plan?

starting-out-talking-to-leela.player: I need to obtain a copy of the key to the Prince's cell, create a disguise for him that makes him look like Keli and then break him out of the jail.

starting-out-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
starting-out-talking-to-leela.text: I'd say that's a good summary. Now, do you have any questions for me about any part of the plan?

options.text: Any ideas for the key?

steps.player: Any ideas for the key?

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Keli keeps it on her at all times, on a chain around her neck. If you can convince her to show it to you, you might be able to use some soft clay to take an imprint.
If the player hasn't obtained the key print yet:

steps.player: That doesn't sound easy.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: My suggestion is that you pretend to be interested in joining her bandits. From there, you should be able to steer the conversation towards the key.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Once you have the imprint, take it to my father along with a bronze bar. He'll then be able to make us a copy.
If the player has the key print in their inventory:

steps.player: I already have the imprint!

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Then you should take it to my father along with a bronze bar. He'll then be able to make us a copy.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Do you have any other questions about the plan?

options.text: Any ideas for the disguise?

steps.player: Any ideas for the disguise?

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: To make the Prince look like Keli, you'll need a blonde wig and a pink skirt. You'll also want some skin paste to hide the black eye he got when they captured him.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: There's an old sailor in the village who makes rope. Perhaps he could make you a wig. Don't forget to dye it once you have one.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: For the skin paste, there's a local witch who's apparently an expert on all sorts of potions. I'm sure she could make you some. I hear she also sells dye, if you need some for the wig.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Finally there's the skirt. I imagine you could just buy one from any clothes shop. Thessalia's Fine Clothes in Varrock is probably the closest.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Do you have any other questions about the plan?

options.text: Don't think so. I'll go and prepare.

steps.player: Don't think so. I'll go and prepare.

starting-out-talking-to-leela-talking-to.speaker: Leela
starting-out-talking-to-leela-talking-to.text: You're back. Do you have everything needed yet?

options.text: Any ideas for the key?
Any ideas for the disguise?
Not yet. I'll go and prepare.

steps.player: Not yet. I'll go and prepare.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-ned.speaker: Ned
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-ned.text: Why, hello there, [lad/lass/kid]. Me friends call me Ned. I was a man of the sea, but it's past me now. Could I be making or selling you some rope?

options.text: Could you make other things apart from rope?

steps.player: Could you make other things apart from rope?

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: I'm sure I can. What are you thinking of?

options.text: Could you knit me a sweater?

steps.player: Could you knit me a sweater?

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Do I look like a member of a sewing circle? Be off wi' you. I have fought monsters that would turn your hair blue.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: I don't need to be laughed at just 'cos I'm getting a bit old.

options.text: How about some sort of wig?

steps.player: How about some sort of wig?

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Well... that's an interesting thought. Yes, I think I could do something. Give me three balls of wool and I might be able to do it.
If the player does not have three balls of wool:

steps.player: Great, I will get some. I think a wig would be useful.

steps.text: If the player has three balls of wool:

options.text: I have them here. Please make me a wig.

steps.player: I have them here. Please make me a wig.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Okay, I'll have a go.
Ned gives you a pretty good wig.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Here you go. How's that for a quick effort? Not bad I think!

steps.player: Thanks Ned. There's more to you than meets the eye.

options.text: Actually, I don't need one right now.

steps.player: Actually, I don't need one right now.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Fair enough.

options.text: Could you repair the arrow holes in the back of my shirt?

steps.player: Could you repair the arrow holes in the back of my shirt?

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Ah yes, it's a tough world these days. There's a few brave enough to attack from ten metres away.
Ned pulls out a needle and attacks your shirt.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: There you go, good as new.

steps.player: Thanks Ned. Maybe next time they will attack me face to face.

options.text: Actually, I don't need anything.

steps.player: Actually, I don't need anything.

options.text: Yes, I would like some rope.
No thanks, Ned. I don't need any.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-aggie.speaker: Aggie
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-aggie.text: What can I help you with?

options.text: What could you make for me?
Can you make skin paste?

steps.player: Can you make skin paste?

steps.text: If the player does not have all the required items:

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Why, it's one of my most popular potions! Lots of people around here like to pretty their faces up a bit. I can make it for you if you get me what's needed.

steps.player: What do you need?

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Well dearie, you need a base for the paste. That's a mix of ash, flour and water. Then you need redberries to colour it as you want. Bring me those four items and I will make you some.
If the player has all the required items:

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Yes I can. I see you already have the ingredients. Would you like me to mix some for you now?

options.text: Yes please. Mix me some skin paste.

steps.player: Yes please. Mix me some skin paste.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: That should be simple. Hand the things to Aggie then.
You hand the ash, flour, water and redberries to Aggie. She tips the ingredients into a cauldron and mutters some words.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Tourniquet, Fenderbaum, Tottenham, Marshmallow, Marblearch.
Aggie hands you the skin paste.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: There you go dearie. That will make you look good at the Varrock dances.

options.text: No thank you. I don't need any skin paste right now.

steps.player: No thank you. I don't need any skin paste right now.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Okay dearie, that's always your choice.

options.text: Cool, do you turn people into frogs?
You mad old witch, you can't help me.
Can you make dyes for me please?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.player: Are you the famous Lady Keli? Leader of the toughest gang of bandits around?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.speaker: Lady Keli
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.text: Yes, I am Keli. You've heard of me then?

options.text: Heard of you? You're famous in Gielinor!

steps.player: Heard of you? You're famous in Gielinor!

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: That's very kind of you to say. Reputations are not easily earned. I have managed to succeed where many fail.

options.text: I think Katrine is still tougher.
options.condition: If Shield of Arrav has been completed:

steps.player: I think Katrine is still tougher.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Well you can think that all you like! Those cowards dare not leave Varrock. Out here, I'm toughest. You can tell them that! Now get out of my sight, before I call my guards.

options.text: What's your latest plan then?

steps.player: What's your latest plan then?

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Why do you want to know?

steps.player: Well I was actually hoping to join your group.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Join us? Interesting... I suppose you do look the type.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: You'll of course need to properly prove yourself before we let you join us. However, what I can tell you is that we currently have a very valuable prisoner. If all goes well, he will make us very rich.

options.text: Ah, I see. You must have been very skillful.

steps.player: Ah, I see. You must have been very skillful.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: To catch him? Oh yes. We had to grab him without his bodyguards noticing. It was a stroke of genius. Mostly my doing, of course.

options.text: How do you know someone won't try to free him?
Well good luck with it.
How do you know someone won't try to free him?

steps.player: How do you know someone won't try to free him?

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: There is no way to release him. The only key to his cell is on a chain around my neck, and the locksmith who made it died very suddenly.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: There isn't another key like this in the world.

options.text: Could I see the key please?

steps.player: Could I see the key please?

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Why?

steps.player: It will be something I can tell my grandchildren, when you are even more famous than you are now.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Well I suppose there's no harm in letting you see it. After all, you have no hope of stealing it.
Keli shows you a small key on a strong looking chain.
If the player doesn't have soft clay or already has the key print:

steps.player: Thank you. I'd better go now.

options.text: Could I touch the key for a moment please?

steps.player: Could I touch the key for a moment please?

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Well... only for a moment then.
As you touch the key, you take an imprint of it using your soft clay.

steps.player: Thank you so much! You are too kind.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: You are welcome, but run along now. I will need some time to consider your request to join us.

options.text: Thank you. I'd better go now.

steps.player: Thank you. I'd better go now.

options.text: That is a good way to keep secrets.

steps.player: That is a good way to keep secrets.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: It is the best way I know. Dead men tell no tales.

options.text: Well I'll be off. Good luck.

steps.player: Well I'll be off. Good luck.

options.text: Well good luck with it.

steps.player: Well good luck with it.

options.text: You must have trained a lot for this work.

steps.player: You must have trained a lot for this work.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: I have used a sword since I was a girl. My first kill was before I was even six years old.

options.text: What's your latest plan then?
I shouldn't disturb someone as tough as you.
I shouldn't disturb someone as tough as you.

steps.player: I shouldn't disturb someone as tough as you.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Yes, I am very busy. Goodbye.

options.text: I've heard a little, but I think Katrine is tougher.
options.condition: If Shield of Arrav has been completed:

options.text: I've heard rumours that you kill people.

steps.player: I've heard rumours that you kill people.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: There's always someone ready to spread rumours. I hear all sort of ridiculous things these days.

options.text: What's your latest plan then?
You must have trained a lot for this work.
I shouldn't disturb someone as tough as you.
No, I've never really heard of you.

steps.player: No, I've never really heard of you.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: You must be new around here then. Everyone knows of Lady Keli and her prowess with a sword.

options.text: No, still doesn't ring a bell.

steps.player: No, still doesn't ring a bell.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Well, you know of me now. You should also know that I will wring your neck if you don't show some respect.

options.text: I don't show respect to killers and hoodlums.

steps.player: I don't show respect to killers and hoodlums.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: You should, you really should. I am wealthy enough to place a bounty on your head, or I could just remove your head myself. Luckily, I am too busy to deal with the likes of you, so clear off!

options.text: What's your latest plan then?
You must have trained a lot for this work.
I shouldn't disturb someone as tough as you.
Actually, I have heard of you. You're famous in Gielinor!

steps.player: Actually, I have heard of you. You're famous in Gielinor!

options.text: You must have trained a lot for this work.
I shouldn't disturb someone as tough as you.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.speaker: Lady Keli
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.text: Oh, it's you. What do you want?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.player: I was hoping we could talk more about your prisoner.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.speaker: Lady Keli
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.text: Until you join us, I can say little. What I can tell you is that he is very valuable. If all goes well, he will make us very rich.

options.text: Ah, I see. You must have been very skillful.
How do you know someone won't try to free him?
Well good luck with it.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-joe.player: Hi. Who are you guarding here?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-joe.speaker: Joe
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-joe.text: Can't say. It's all very secret. You should get out of here. I am not supposed to talk while I guard.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.text: You're back. Do you have everything needed yet?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.text: Good work. Now, before breaking the Prince out, you'll need to find a way to deal with his personal guard. He's talkative, so try to find a weakness. Remember, we don't want any unneeded violence.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.player: Alright. I'll go have a chat to this guard.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.text: You're back. How are things going?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.player: I'm afraid I lost that key you gave me.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.text: Well that was foolish. I can sort you out with another, but it will cost you 15 coins.
If the player does not have 15 coins:

steps.player: I haven't got that much.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Then come back to me when you do.

steps.player: Here, I have 15 coins.

steps.text: Leela gives you a key.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Now, how are things going with that guard?

steps.player: I haven't spoken to him yet.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Well you'd better get on it then. We need him out of the way.

options.text: I have some beer here. Fancy one?

steps.player: I have some beer here. Fancy one?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Ah, that would be lovely. Only one though, just to wet my throat.

steps.player: Of course. It must be tough being here without a drink.

steps.text: You hand a beer to the guard. He drinks it in seconds.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: That was perfect! I can't thank you enough.

steps.player: How are you? Still okay? Not too drunk?

steps.text: If the player has less than three beers:

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: No, I don't get drunk from only one drink. I reckon I'd need at least two more for that. Still, thanks for the beer.
If the player has two more beers:

steps.player: Would you care for another beer, my friend?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: I'd better not. I don't want to be drunk on duty.

steps.player: Here, just keep these for later. I hate to see a thirsty guard.

steps.text: You hand two more beers to the guard. He takes a sip of one, and then he quickly drinks them both.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Franksh! That wash jusht what I need to shtay on guard. No more beersh, I don't want to get drunk.

options.text: Tell me about the life of a guard.

steps.player: Tell me about the life of a guard.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Well, the hours are good, but most of those hours are a drag.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Sometimes I wonder if I should have spent more time learning when I was a young boy. Maybe I wouldn't be here now, scared of Keli.

options.text: What did you want to be when you were a boy?
I'd better go.
What did you want to be when you were a boy?

steps.player: What did you want to be when you were a boy?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Well, I loved to sit by the lake, with my toes in the water. I'd shoot the fish with my bow and arrow.

steps.player: That's a strange hobby for a boy.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: It kept us from goblin hunting, which was what most boys did.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Hang on... Why do you ask? What do you want?

options.text: Hey, chill out. I won't cause you trouble.

steps.player: Hey, chill out. I won't cause you trouble.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Sorry, it's hard to relax when I'm on duty. Stress of the job, and all.

steps.player: So why do you do it?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: There's good money in it, and some of the shouting I rather like.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: RESISTANCE IS USELESS!

options.text: So what do you buy with your great wages?

steps.player: So what do you buy with your great wages?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Really, after working here, there's only time for a drink or three. All us guards go to the same pub and drink ourselves stupid.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: It's what I enjoy these days. I can't resist the sight of a really cold beer.

options.text: I have some beer here. Fancy one?
Tell me about the life of a guard.
What did you want to be when you were a boy?
I'd better go.
Tell me about the life of a guard.
Would you be interested in making a little more money?

steps.player: Would you be interested in making a little more money?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: What? Are you trying to bribe me? I may not be a great guard, but I am loyal. How dare you try to bribe me!

steps.player: No, no, you've got the wrong idea, totally. I just wondered if you wanted some part-time bodyguard work.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Oh... sorry. No, I don't need money. As long as you were not offering me a bribe.

options.text: I'd better go.
Tell me about the life of a guard.
I'd better go.
I'd better go.

steps.player: I'd better go.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Thanks, I appreciate that. Talking on duty can be punished by having your mouth stitched up. These are tough people, make no mistake.

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-joe-talk.player: Hello friend. I'm just here to rescue the Prince, if thats okay?

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-joe-talk.speaker: Joe
executing-the-rescue-talking-to-joe-talk.text: Thatsh a funny joke. You are lucky I'm shober. Go in peace, friend.

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-leela-ag.speaker: Leela
executing-the-rescue-talking-to-leela-ag.text: You're back. How are things going with that guard?

options.text: I could attack him.

prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman

prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-prince-ali.text: Good to see you, friend. I am forever in your debt for what you did, as is all of Al Kharid.

prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-prince-ali.text: I know my father is very grateful as well. If he were in better health, he would have thanked you personally. However, at his age, it is best that he spends his time resting.

prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-chancellor.text: Prince Ali is home safe. You have the eternal gratitude of the Emir for rescuing his son. Please, take this payment as a thank you.
